models_evaluated: custom domain-specific AI model fine-tuned on institutional data

links.outcome: Preference for AI impressions by original vs independent radiologists and oncologists
links.effect: Original radiologists slightly preferred their own impressions to the custom model (h = 0.18, p = 0.0716), while independent radiologists showed no preference (h = -0.03, p = 0.78). Both groups rated generic model impressions lower.
links.quote: Original radiologists slightly preferred their own impressions to the custom model (h = 0.18, p = 0.0716), while independent radiologists showed no preference (h = -0.03, p = 0.78).

links.outcome: Comparison of custom AI, generic LLM and radiologist impressions on completeness, correctness, and utility
links.effect: Custom model achieved near parity with human impressions; generic LLM impressions were less preferred by radiologists (h 1.04-1.22 original; 0.66-0.69 independent, p < 0.001) and less concise (r = 0.85-0.87).
links.quote: Custom model impressions achieved near parity with human impressions; original radiologists rated their own impressions slightly more complete (r = 0.22, p = 0.0016).

unlisted_practices: Fine-tuning a domain-specific model on institutional data versus using a general-purpose LLM for radiology impression generation

screen.reason: Empirical multi-stakeholder reader study evaluating custom fine-tuned LLM vs generic LLM vs human radiologist impressions on clinical utility and safety, without testing a specific deployment practice/safeguard.
